_readme: Golden output for bitwrench's string-generating APIs.
Each case is TACO in, exact HTML out. Not substring checks -- exact.
A substring check cannot see a removal, and that is precisely how the
v2.1.0 handler regression reached six releases: the guard on that API was
assert.ok(html.includes('bw_fn_0')), which is satisfied by BOTH
so it passed while the handler quietly disappeared from the output.
If a diff shows up here, that is the point. Read it and decide whether the
change was intended. Do not regenerate to make the suite green.
To accept an intended change: UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 npm run test:golden
then commit the diff so it appears in review and in the release notes.

cases.name: text content is escaped by default
cases.why: Escaping is the default so that untrusted content cannot become markup. bw.raw() is the deliberate opt-out. If this ever emits live tags, that is an XSS hole, not a formatting change.

cases.name: nesting and attributes
cases.why: The shape of TACO -> HTML. Arrays nest, a is attributes, c is content. This is the contract every generated page depends on.

cases.name: style object becomes a CSS string
cases.why: Styles are data. camelCase must convert to kebab-case -- browsers silently ignore camelCase in a style attribute, so getting this wrong fails invisibly (it did once; see commit 50a4555).

cases.name: boolean attribute
cases.why: true renders as a bare attribute, not ="true". false and null drop out entirely.

cases.name: self-closing tag
cases.why: Void elements must not get a closing tag or the HTML parser produces a different tree than intended.

cases.name: function handler auto-registers and emits a dispatch call
cases.why: THE north-star case for bw.html(). See test/bitwrench_test_html_page.js for the full argument. In short: bw.html(taco) -> HTML must be one call. A function in, a working handler out, no binding step. v2.1.0 replaced this with a silent drop unless the caller passed {fns}, which broke every bare bw.html() carrying a handler. If this line changes, you are changing that contract -- go read the WHY block in the test file before you touch it.

cases.name: string handler passes through escaped, no registry involved
cases.why: A string on* is the author's own inline JS. It is escaped but not registered -- only functions get the dispatch treatment.

cases.name: fns registry emits a class marker and nothing executable
cases.why: The CSP-safe path, used by bw.htmlPage(). No on* attribute may appear here -- an inline handler violates a strict script-src, which is the whole reason this path exists. If an onclick shows up in this line, CSP output is broken.

cases.name: URLs in attributes are not slash-escaped
cases.why: escapeHTML escapes / -- an OWASP rule for element content, where it blunts a stray '</script'. Inside an attribute value / is ordinary, and escaping it emitted https://example.com for every href, src and action. Browsers decode it so links worked, which is why it survived; it was wrong for anything diffing or greping server-rendered HTML, and it appeared verbatim in the tutorial panel that claims to show the HTML you would have written by hand. Note the semantic equivalence test cannot see this -- both forms parse to the same value -- so this exact string is the guard.

cases.name: attribute values still escape what actually matters
cases.why: Dropping / must not become dropping the rest. & and " are mandatory inside a double-quoted attribute -- without them a value can terminate the attribute and inject another one. < and > are escaped too, which is stricter than required and stricter than the DOM's own serialiser.

cases.name: content escaping is unchanged, / included
cases.why: The relaxation is scoped to attributes. Element content keeps the full set, so this case is the tripwire for anyone tempted to 'simplify' by pointing both contexts at one escaper again -- which is exactly how the attribute bug existed.

pages.name: htmlPage skeleton with no runtime
pages.why: The document contract: doctype first, lang, charset, escaped title. Anything that changes this changes every standalone page and every embedded dashboard served from a device.

pages.name: htmlPage escapes the title
pages.why: The title is the one place user text lands in <head>. Unescaped, it breaks out of the tag.
